record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.context_brief: Eta-helium-3 bound state versus virtual state
record.original_question: Does the eta-helium-3 system realize a near-threshold eta-nucleus bound state or a virtual state? A resolution should determine the sign of the real part of the eta-helium-3 scattering length using sufficiently accurate below-threshold data, such as inelastic-channel measurements or high-statistics gamma helium-3 to pi-zero p X data, because existing analyses of TAPS/MAMI data favored the virtual-state scenario but could not exclude a bound state.

evidence.quote: However, to make this analysis useful we need to know, if a bound state exists or not.
Since the existing data is not of sufficient accuracy and there is currently no new measurement planed, we will not describe this here in detail.
Thus the data prefers the solution that corresponds to a virtual state, although the existence of a bound state can not be excluded, given the quality of the data.
The expected much higher statistics promise for a near future an unambiguous decision on what scenario is realized: a bound state or a virtual state.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the near-threshold interaction of an η meson with a ³He nucleus. The s-wave η–³He scattering length a = Re(a) + i Im(a) governs the low-energy behavior of the elastic amplitude; a pole of the amplitude on the physical sheet corresponds to a genuine bound state of the η–³He system, while a pole on the unphysical sheet corresponds to a virtual (antibound) state. Existing final-state-interaction analyses of η-production data near threshold determine |Re(a)| ≈ 4 fm with appreciable Im(a), but are insensitive to the sign of Re(a); a negative sign would indicate a virtual state, while a positive sign (with sufficient magnitude) would indicate a true near-threshold bound state.

Problem. Determine whether the η–³He system supports a genuine near-threshold bound state or only a virtual state, equivalently: determine the sign of Re(a) for the η–³He s-wave scattering length, using sufficiently accurate sub-threshold information (for example, inelastic-channel cross sections such as γ ³He → π⁰ p X, or other observables sensitive to the analytic structure below threshold).
artifact.status_search_result: As of recent searches (WASA-at-COSY 2020 results and a 2023 few-body theoretical study), the question remains unresolved. WASA-at-COSY analyses of pd→³He 2γ/6γ found only a slight indication of a possible bound-state signal and could not decisively distinguish bound from virtual scenarios. Final-state-interaction analyses fix |Re(a)| ≈ 4.2 fm but cannot determine the sign of Re(a). Theoretical few-body calculations probing η³He continue to debate the binding question.

status_evidence.title: Search for η mesic 3He with the WASA-at-COSY facility
status_evidence.snippet: Slight indication for a possible bound state signal; width Γ > 20 MeV, binding energy 0–15 MeV; not conclusive.
status_evidence.claim: The bound-state vs virtual-state question for η-³He has not been definitively settled experimentally.

status_evidence.title: Probing the existence of η³He mesic nucleus with a few-body approach
status_evidence.snippet: Few-body theoretical study of η³He system, 2023, continues to investigate existence of bound state.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of an η³He bound state remains an open theoretical question as of 2023.

status_evidence.title: Status of the Search for η-Mesic Nuclei with Focus on η-Helium Bound States
status_evidence.snippet: Review (2020) of the status of η-mesic nuclei searches including η-³He; sign of Re(a) not determined by final-state interaction alone.
status_evidence.claim: Sign of Re(a) for η-³He scattering length is not determined by current data.
